evidence.quote:
Kibuuka Omumbaale
2 October – 6 December 2026
Chisenhale Gallery presents Kibuuka Omumbaale, a major new video commission and the first UK exhibition by Kampala-based collective Wakaliga Uganda.
Wednesday–Sunday, 12–6pm
64 Chisenhale Road, London, E3 5QZ

listing.blurb: An exhibition at Chisenhale Gallery, the artist-founded space on Chisenhale Road, featuring Wakaliga Uganda. It runs into early December, so there's no rush.

history.change: wrote the story: who, then, now, vibe, worth_knowing
cut unsupported details: 'new video commission', 'several panel discussions'

story.who: Wakaliga Uganda are a film collective from Kampala, and this is their first UK exhibition, according to the gallery's own website. Isaac Nabwana and Harriet Nakasujja set up the collective, which runs a film studio in the city's Wakaliga district. Their shows include If Uganda Was America at The Renaissance Society in Chicago in 2025 and documenta fifteen in Kassel in 2022, and their films were screened at MoMA in New York in 2019.
story.then: The gallery's own website says the group has a cult reputation for films that rework Western action films, as well as Cantonese martial arts cinema and online viral video. Cast and crew build props, costumes and sets from found materials. They also teach one another martial arts and CGI, and help write the scripts.
story.now: The show was co-commissioned by the gallery and The Santozeum in Santorini. It starts from the 1961 return of the remains of Kibuuka Omumbaale, a Buganda warrior-god, out of Cambridge University and back to the Uganda Museum in Kampala. In the film a teenager, Isaak, gains the god's powers after a school trip to the museum.
story.vibe: The gallery's own website describes a subversive superhero action film with a playful, incisive tone. It borrows the Ugandan VJ tradition, where a comic narrator, called a 'video joker', improvises over the action, and draws on Hong Kong martial arts cinema.
worth_knowing: The film weaves its story together with remarks from elders, healers and museum guides.
A talk between Isaac Nabwana and Ryan Trecartin and a panel discussion are also part of the programme.
